provisioning.managed.dashboard: This dashboard comes from the set “{set}”. Change its file and apply it with kalzit provision apply, and it changes here. In the interface it is read-only.
provisioning.managed.datasource: This data source comes from the set “{set}”. Change its file, then apply. In the interface it is read-only.
provisioning.managed.role: The permissions of this role are in a file of the set “{set}”. In the interface they are read-only.
provisioning.managed.alertRule: This rule comes from the set “{set}”. Change its file, then apply. In the interface it is read-only.
provisioning.outside.dashboard: Sharing, annotations, reports and silences are not part of the file and keep working.
provisioning.outside.datasource: Testing and the AI access are not part of the file and keep working.
provisioning.outside.role: Members are still assigned here or through groups; the file sets only the permissions.
provisioning.outside.alertRule: Pausing and silencing are not part of the file and keep working.
provisioning.popover.unlocked: Unlocked since {date}. The next apply overwrites changes and locks it again.
provisioning.popover.drifted: Differs from its file. The next apply overwrites that.
provisioning.unlock.title: Unlock “{name}”?
provisioning.unlock.from: The resource comes from this file. Once unlocked it can be changed here, in an emergency for example.
provisioning.unlock.drift: The change counts as drift and is listed under Administration > Provisioning.
provisioning.unlock.overwrite: The next apply overwrites it from the file and locks it again.
provisioning.unlock.keep: To keep the change, put it into the file.
provisioning.unlock.done: “{name}” unlocked. That is in the audit log.
provisioning.drift.title: Drift
provisioning.drift.lead: The next apply overwrites it from the files.
provisioning.drift.unlockedText: Unlocked on {date}; changes in the interface are possible. File:
provisioning.drift.missingText: Deleted on the server. The next apply creates the resource again. File:
provisioning.drift.driftedText: On the server it differs from what was applied last. File:
provisioning.applies.title: Applies
provisioning.applies.lead: From the audit log. Plan runs and rejected applies change nothing and are not listed.
provisioning.applies.none: No apply in the audit log yet.
provisioning.list.title: Managed resources
provisioning.list.footnote: Sets are applied with kalzit provision apply, never here. Unlocking is for emergencies and is in the audit log.
provisioning.empty.title: Nothing from files yet
provisioning.empty.text: Keep dashboards, data sources, roles and alert rules as files in Git and apply them from the command line. The easiest start is an export of what is already there.
provisioning.empty.tip: Tip: run plan --exit-code on every pull request. Changes then show in the review before anyone applies them.
provisioning.import.title: Import a Grafana dashboard
provisioning.import.lead: From a JSON file as Grafana writes it on export. Kalzit reads only the description, runs nothing and installs no plugins. What it cannot take over exactly shows in the report before anything is created.
provisioning.import.drop: Drag a JSON file here or choose one
provisioning.import.notJson: This is not valid JSON. Check that the file is complete and no comma or bracket is missing.
provisioning.import.notDashboard: This is not a dashboard: the file has neither panels nor rows. Only dashboards can be imported here.
provisioning.import.tooLarge: The file is larger than 5 MB.
provisioning.import.unreadable: The import cannot read this file. Export the dashboard from Grafana as classic JSON.
provisioning.import.libraryPanels: Library panels that are only references in the file: {count}. Export the dashboard with embedded panels, or import without them: they end up as “skipped”.
provisioning.import.oldSchema: Schema version {version} is old. Kalzit reads it but approximates more. Check the summary closely.
provisioning.import.name: Dashboard name
provisioning.import.rights: This needs dashboards:write in the target folder. For folders managed by files there is kalzit provision import-grafana.
provisioning.import.sourcesLead: Only sources open to you are listed. Queries are taken over word for word; Kalzit reads macros such as $__timeFilter and $__interval the same way.
provisioning.import.leftOutHint: Without a source, the panels of that source are left out, with the reason in the summary. They can be rebuilt later on another source.
provisioning.import.variableHint: Kalzit has no variables that pick a data source. Their panels use the chosen source for good.
provisioning.import.reportLeadBefore: Nothing is created until the import runs.
provisioning.import.createsTop: Panels to create outside every folder: {count}
provisioning.import.forbidden: Creating dashboards in “{folder}” is closed to this account, or one of the sources is. Choose a folder with dashboards:write, or ask an admin.
provisioning.import.reportLead: Imported from Grafana: “{source}”, on {date}. This report stays with the dashboard.
provisioning.import.noReportText: This dashboard was made another way.
provisioning.notice.text: Imported from Grafana on {date}. Panels created: {created}, of them approximated: {approximated}, left out: {skipped}.
provisioning.note.variable_formats: Variable formats such as ${name:csv} were dropped; Kalzit passes variable values as parameters.
provisioning.note.sql_macro: {macro} has no counterpart in Kalzit. Rewrite that part of the query before it runs.
provisioning.note.query_builder: Built with Grafana’s query builder, so there is no query text to take over.
provisioning.note.query_builder_sql: Built with Grafana’s query builder, so there is no SQL text to take over.
provisioning.note.legend_format: The legend format is not taken over; series keep their label names.
provisioning.note.time_series_format: Grafana’s time series format is not taken over; the query answers a table.
provisioning.note.aggregations: Metric and bucket aggregations are not taken over; the query answers documents.
provisioning.note.source_kind: Queries of Kalzit data sources of type {kind} are not converted.
provisioning.note.grafana_source: {source} is Grafana’s own and has no counterpart in Kalzit.
provisioning.note.no_mapping: No Kalzit data source was chosen for {source}.
provisioning.note.no_mapping_default: No Kalzit data source was chosen for the default data source.
provisioning.note.ref_id: Its refId is used twice or is too long.
provisioning.note.unit_too_long: The unit is too long and was dropped.
provisioning.note.threshold_colors: Threshold colors without a counterpart became neutral.
provisioning.note.value_mappings: Value mappings are not taken over.
provisioning.note.overrides: Field overrides are not taken over.
provisioning.note.gradient: The gradient display became the basic one.
provisioning.note.html_text: HTML content is shown as plain text.
provisioning.note.text_cut: The text was cut to {max} characters.
provisioning.note.library_panel: A library panel: its content is not in the dashboard JSON.
provisioning.note.graph_panel: The old graph panel became a time series; its own display options are not taken over.
provisioning.note.singlestat_panel: The old singlestat panel became a stat panel.
provisioning.note.table_panel: The old table panel became a table; its column styles are not taken over.
provisioning.note.piechart_panel: The pie chart plugin became the pie chart panel.
provisioning.note.heatmap_buckets: The heatmap’s bucket options are not taken over.
provisioning.note.node_graph: The node graph became a network panel; it needs a graph-shaped result.
provisioning.note.panel_type: Kalzit has no counterpart of the panel type {type}.
provisioning.note.no_queries: None of its queries could be converted.
provisioning.note.grid_fitted: Its place was fitted into the 24 columns.
provisioning.note.time_shift: The time shift {shift} is not a plain length and was dropped.
provisioning.note.repeat_dropped: The repeat over {variable} was dropped: that variable does not take several values here.
provisioning.note.panel_link: The link {title} was dropped: its address is not http, https, mailto or a path.
provisioning.note.options_default: The options fell back to the defaults because Kalzit could not take them over.
provisioning.note.options_default_field: The options fell back to the defaults because the value of {field} did not fit.
provisioning.note.variable_name: Its name is not a Kalzit variable name (letters, digits, _).
provisioning.note.variable_helper: Grafana’s {helper} helper has no counterpart in Kalzit.
provisioning.note.variable_regex: The regex filter of the values is not taken over.
provisioning.note.auto_interval: The automatic interval option is not taken over.
provisioning.note.variable_datasource: Variables that pick a data source come later in Kalzit.
provisioning.note.variable_adhoc: Ad hoc filters come later in Kalzit.
provisioning.note.variable_type: Kalzit has no counterpart of the variable type {type}.
provisioning.note.all_option: The “All” option is not taken over.
provisioning.note.builtin_annotations: Grafana’s built-in annotations stay in Grafana.
provisioning.note.link_no_tag: A link to dashboards without a tag.
provisioning.note.link_first_tag: Only the first tag ({tag}) is kept.
provisioning.note.link_invalid: It needs a title and an http, https, mailto or path address.
provisioning.note.link_type: Links of type {type} are not converted.
provisioning.note.row_layout: The old row layout was placed on the 24-column grid.
provisioning.note.time_range: The time range could not be read and is the last 6 hours.
provisioning.note.refresh: The refresh {refresh} is outside 5 seconds to a day and was dropped.
provisioning.note.time_zone: The time zone {zone} is not known and was dropped.
provisioning.note.step_dropped: Grafana’s {kind} has no Kalzit step and was left out.
provisioning.note.step_merge: Merge became “Stack tables”: rows with equal values are not combined into one.
provisioning.note.step_reducer: The calculation {reducer} has no counterpart and was left out.
provisioning.note.step_conversion: The conversion of {field} to {type} has no counterpart and was left out.
provisioning.note.step_time_format: The time format {format} uses parts Kalzit does not read; ISO 8601 is read instead.
provisioning.note.step_matcher: The condition {matcher} on {field} has no counterpart and was left out.
provisioning.note.step_empty: Grafana’s {kind} had nothing Kalzit could take over and was left out.
provisioning.note.step_reducer_row: Grafana’s {reducer} became the cell of that row, which may be empty; Kalzit’s first and last value skip empty cells.
provisioning.note.step_reducer_sample: Grafana computes {reducer} over all values (population); Kalzit uses the sample (n − 1).
provisioning.note.step_pattern_flags: The pattern {pattern} uses the flags {flags}, which Kalzit does not read; the step was left out.
